events.title: NYRR Open Run: St. Marys Park
events.description: NYRR Open Run brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.St. Mary's Park offers a wonderful respite from the hustle and bustle of urban life. Located in the Mott Haven neighborhood in the South Bronx, the park features rolling hills, expanses of green grass, and grand old trees. The site was once part of the estate of Jonas Bronck (1600-43), for whom the Bronx is named. It is one of the largest parks in the area with a pool, playground, basketball courts, an indoor recreation center, picnic seating areas, and more. In the winter, the hills are perfect for sledding. St. Mary’s Park received $30 million from NYC’s Anchor Parks initiative, which will renovate the park’s ballfields, pathways, and amphitheater.

events.title: Cuidado de Árboles y Arbustos para Jardineros Comunitarios
events.description: Únase a GreenThumb para un Taller Práctico de Cuidado de Árboles en el jardín comunitario. Juntos, exploraremos los árboles y arbustos del jardín mientras aprendemos maneras prácticas de identificar árboles, evaluar su salud, reconocer señales de estrés o enfermedad, comprender sus necesidades de agua y del lugar donde crecen, y practicar técnicas básicas de poda y mantenimiento. También dedicaremos un momento a conectarnos con los árboles como elementos fundamentales del ecosistema del jardín: desde sus raíces y ramas hasta sus flores, frutos, semillas, aves e insectos. El taller concluirá con la participación de todos en la plantación y el riego de un nuevo árbol de serbal de servicio (serviceberry), seguido de una breve reflexión colectiva para darle la bienvenida al árbol al jardín.Esta sesión está abierta a cualquier persona que hable inglés, ya que tanto nuestro facilitador como el personal son bilingües.Regístrate AquíNYC Parks GreenThumb organiza este evento. Nos enorgullece ser el programa de jardinería comunitaria urbana más grande del país, apoyando a más de 550 jardines comunitarios en toda la Ciudad de Nueva York. Con el apoyo de GreenThumb, los jardines comunitarios son espacios que promueven la justicia ambiental y contribuyen a que nuestra ciudad sea más equitativa, segura y verde para todas las personas. Los eventos de GreenThumb son gratuitos y están abiertos al público.

events.title: Working with Rain: A Rain Garden Workshop

The public will also have the opportunity to sign up for the DEP program, which will provide all necessary equipment and materials for performing maintenance activities stewarding a rain garden.Register HereNYC Parks GreenThumb hosts this event. We are proud to be the nation’s most extensive urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

events.title: Seeds of Restoration: Collecting Native Seeds for Biodiversity
events.description: This workshop introduces attendees to the importance of seed collection for the conservation and propagation of native plant species in NYC. Led by staff from the NYC Parks Plant Ecology Center and Nursery, participants will learn about the importance of plant habitat to local ecosystems and how seed-based restoration promotes biodiversity. They will participate in a seed-collection walk through northern Central Park and learn about the common native plants of New York City. All materials will be provided, though attendees should be prepared to walk off-trail in Central Park, where there may be ticks and poison ivy. Bug spray, drinking water, and long pants are recommended.Register HereNYC Parks GreenThumb hosts this event. events.title: Forest Fitness
events.description: Join us for a free, year-round “Fitness at the Fort” exercise program on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays!This fitness class incorporates climbing multiple staircases, stretches and strengthening exercises, notable tree identification, and forest bathing. events.title: Candlelight Ghost Tours
events.description: Doors slam, floorboards creak, voices call into the dead of night. Venture into “Manhattan’s Most Haunted House” by flickering candlelight to hear chilling – and true – tales of decades of otherworldly activity in the house, the results of years of paranormal investigations – and the latest stunning scientific findings.The Tredwell family lived at 29 East 4th Street for nearly 100 years, and at least eight people died in the house. Reports of strange and inexplicable occurrences have been widespread since Gertrude, the last surviving Tredwell, died in 1933. Is it Gertrude who is watching over her family home? Join us and decide for yourself.50-minute tours begin every half hour, 6:30 to 9 p.m.

events.title: Super Spooky Candlelight Ghost Tours with Paranormal Investigator Dan Sturges
events.description: In 2020, the museum closed due to COVID-19, leaving the house empty of staff and visitors. Dan Sturges, who has undertaken paranormal investigations at the Merchant’s House for 15 years, teamed up with neuroscientist Dr. Lee to conduct scientific research using specialized equipment custom-built for the house. Mounting fact-based evidence points to the very likely reality of paranormal activity at the Merchant’s House.Join paranormal investigator Dan Sturges on a 90-minute In-Person Super Spooky Candlelight Ghost Tour for an in-depth look at the latest research and findings. Dan is the founder of Sturges Paranormal and appears on the Travel Channel’s weekly series, Paranormal Caught on Camera. He has performed investigations at the Merchant’s House – and documented his spine-chilling findings – since 2007.90-minute tour begins 9:30 p.m.

events.title: BHS's 25th Annual Totten Trot 5K Foot Race
events.description: The Bayside Historical Society will celebrate the milestone Silver Anniversary of its annual Totten Trot 5K Foot Race and Kids' Fun Run in 2026. What began as a humble gathering of just 12 runners at Fort Totten Park has grown into a vibrant community event, bringing together more than 300 runners — along with their families and teams — for an unforgettable day.Our Totten Trot 5K Foot Race is a Halloween-themed, waterfront course in historic Fort Totten Park on Little Neck Bay in Bayside, a pristine stretch surrounding a preserved Civil War fortress. Runners will pass through the Historic District, which consists of buildings dating to the late 1800s. The Fort is situated where the Long Island Sound meets the East River at the Throgs Neck Bridge. The race starts and finishes at the landmarked Officers' Club, home of Bayside Historical Society. The course includes a loop out onto Little Bay Path to the Throgs Neck Bridge and back to the Fort. Timing and scoring are provided by elitefeats on a USATF Certified Course. Registration begins at 7:30am; the race starts at 9:00am.The Kids' Fun Run is a short-distance sprint for tiny tots and kids up to 12, grouped by age category. Special “Cookie Medals” for participants in the Fun Run! Sign up on race day; the race starts at 10:00am.Halloween costumes are highly encouraged for adults and kids!SPECIAL GUESTS: BHS is excited to welcome back the 501st Legion's Empire City Garrison, a worldwide Star Wars costuming organization, for a special guest appearance at the Totten Trot's silver anniversary event. Don't miss the chance to pose for photos with some of your favorite Star Wars characters!Get complete information about the Totten Trot and find out how to register online at www.baysidehistorical.org/totten-trot-5k-foot-race.
events.venue: Bayside Historical Society (in Fort Totten Park)

events.title: Saunksquas, Sassafras, and Moccasins: Walking Tour with Oleana Whispering Dove
events.description: Join Oleana Whispering Dove for a walking tour on the Wave Hill Grounds, highlighting the rich legacy of the region’s Indigenous Saunksquas and the profound impact of these women throughout history. This tour reflects on historical imprint of known figures like Sojourner Truth, Maya Angelou, Condoleezza Rice, Susan B. Anthony, Matilda Cage, Lucretia Mott, and Gloria Steinem with earlier unsung female leaders known as Saunk Squa’s; Mama Nuchwe, Dostou, Wastawancett, Lyssie, Annetie Pownock. These Native American women held the highest-ranking leadership roles in their communities and were honored by European settlers with titles like Her Royal Majesty, The King’s Queen, and Indian Princess—recognizing their powerful status and influence as they played a pivotal role in governing their regional tribes, leading land negotiations, and signing land treaties. Walks follow a route along mixed-material pathways with varying elevations. A limited amount of walking sticks are available to borrow. Pace varies from a slow walk to moderate walk throughout.

events.title: The Art of Noticing: A Mindful Birding Experience
events.description: Join nature educator Ryan Mandelbaum and yoga/mindfulness instructor Susie Caramanica to explore how mindfulness can deepen our awareness, observation, and enjoyment of the natural world. This guided experience combines mindfulness practices with birding, inviting participants to slow down, clear mental distractions, and become more fully attentive to the environment around them. Through simple grounding exercises, participants will cultivate a focused awareness that can help them notice more—from a bird's song to subtle movement in the canopy, participants can fully appreciate an encounter that might otherwise go unnoticed. The program begins with gentle mindfulness practices designed to settle the mind and sharpen sensory awareness. Participants will then be guided through the landscape, learning to identify birds by sight and sound while observing behavior, habitat, migration, and seasonal activity. No prior experience with birding or mindfulness practice is necessary. Participants are encouraged to wear comfortable clothing and bring water and binoculars if they have them. Registration encouraged; online or by calling 718.549.3200 x251; drop-ins based on availability. Questions? Please contact us at information@wavehill.org or by calling the number and extension provided above. Following this program, join us for Yoga in the Garden with instructor Susie Caramanica (additional fees apply).Additional Fall 2026 Birding programs:Sun, Nov 8: November BirdingWalks follow a route along mixed-material pathways with varying elevations. A limited amount of walking sticks are available to borrow. Pace varies from a slow walk to moderate walk throughout.

events.title: Meet the Artists: Melanie Brewster and Noormah Jamal
events.description: Join us for a Meet the Artist program with exhibiting artists Melanie Brewster and Noormah Jamal. At 2PM, Brewster will be in conversation with Curator of Visual Arts, Rachel Raphaela Gugelberger, to discuss her Sunroom project, A Metaphysical Quest for the Deepest Backbend. This exhibition constructs a metafictional world in which a woman’s yoga practice has become so extreme that she transforms into an ouroboros: a serpent consuming its own tail, a symbol of cyclical time and eternal return. The exhibition takes place in the aftermath of this transformation, and Brewster aims to reflect on extreme wellness practices, the limits of enlightenment, and questions of access within contemporary wellness industries. At 3PM, Jamal will discuss her outdoor installation, Blooms, and activate the site with a collaborative poetry reading with NYU professor and poet Sonya Posmentier. In Blooms, flowering ceramic heads emerge from an arid landscape. These heads represent the resilience of a people through times of hardship, paying specific homage to Jamal's home of Peshawar, Pakistan. Once known as “City of Flowers,” over the years, Peshawar has become dry, mountainous city, and the people and landscape have both endured the effects of climate change and war. Still, the people persevere in their homeland, becoming the city’s flowers. Meet the Artist is an ongoing series of conversations between exhibiting artists, the curatorial team, and sometimes invited guests at Wave Hill. As part of the Sunroom Project Space, this program is designed collaboratively with the artists and takes various forms. Meet the Artist offers visitors, the artists’ communities, and others an opportunity to gain insight into the artist's creative process and the themes present in their work. Registration encouraged but not required, online or by calling 718.549.3200 x251.

events.title: Meet the Artists: Dots and Loops
events.description: Join us for a series of participatory events and workshops with exhibiting artists Jen Chen-Su Huang, Rita Maas, and Audra Wolowiec, whose work is display in the Wave Hill House exhibition Dots and Loops. Dots and Loops presents works that respond to the idea of language as score, exploring its relationship to the natural world through metaphor and meditation. This Meet the Artist event will blend performance, textile-making, and meditative drawing, as each artist conducts a hands-on activity based on their respective artistic practices. Meet the Artist is an ongoing series of conversations between exhibiting artists, the curatorial team, and sometimes invited guests at Wave Hill. The program offers visitors, the artists’ community, and others an opportunity to hear from the artist and gain deeper insight into their work.

events.description: The Fort Tryon Park Conservancy hosts volunteer opportunities for you, your friends, and family to dig in the dirt! Join us to help protect Fort Tryon Park’s ecology and beauty! Meet the NYC Parks’ horticulture staff at the Heather Garden’s Margaret Corbin Circle entrance to sign in at 10:00AM. Activities will include removing debris and weeds and preparing the site for plantings. Tools and gloves will be provided, but wear long pants, sturdy shoes, a face mask as needed, and bring a filled water bottle,Groups of 5+ RSVP by emailing john.kelly@parks.nyc.gov two weeks in advance so we can provide sufficient equipment and tools on hand.Volunteers under 18 must be accompanied by an adult.Stewardship Days along the southwest area of Fort Tryon Park take place on the 3rd Sunday of each month from April to November.
events.venue: Margaret Corbin Circle (in Fort Tryon Park)

events.title: Historic New York: Italian Heritage Walk
events.description: Benvenuti a tutti! Join the Urban Park Ranger as we explore the history and culture of Italian-Americans on Staten Island. Follow along as we walk and talk about some important figures from historical explorers to pop culture phenomena, as well as engage with some activities familiar to Italian tradition.

events.title: Open House New York: Fort Totten Battery
events.description: The Urban Park Rangers will guide you through this civil war era fort, designed to defend our city. Learn more about the history and significance of this site. Visit OHNY to register.
events.venue: Fort Totten Park Visitors Center (in Fort Totten Park)

events.title: Open House New York: Fort Totten Battery
events.description: The Urban Park Rangers will guide you through this civil war era fort, designed to defend our city. Learn more about the history and significance of this site. Visit OHNY to register.
events.venue: Fort Totten Park Visitors Center (in Fort Totten Park)

events.title: Historic New York: Sylvan Grove Cemetery
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers and the Friends of Abandoned Cemeteries of Staten Island for an in-depth look at one of Staten Island’s historic burial grounds. Rangers will share the stories, significance, and cultural history of the site, highlighting the people and events that shaped the surrounding community. Participants will take part in a light stewardship activity by helping remove vines from protected tombstones, supporting ongoing efforts to preserve these important landmarks.
events.venue: Victory Boulevard and Alberta Avenue (in Sylvan Grove Cemetery)

events.title: Nocturnal Seining and Shore Exploration
events.description: Our experienced Urban Park Rangers teach the ecology of our waterways on every seining program. Get ready to get your hands wet; seining programs use nets to catch fish. All equipment is provided; this program is recommended for ages 8 years and older. Join the Urban Park Rangers and explore what creatures live below the waves at night in the intertidal zone of the East River.
events.venue: Fort Totten Front Gate (in Fort Totten Park)

events.title: Healthy Hike
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers for a relaxing, easy walk along the paved paths of Silver Lake Park. This gentle hike is ideal for all ages and abilities, offering a chance to enjoy fresh air, light exercise, and the park’s scenic views at a comfortable pace.
events.venue: Forest Avenue and Silver Lake Park Road (in Silver Lake Park)

events.title: Celtic Halloween Tree Tales
events.description: Celebrate the Halloween season with the Urban Park Rangers as we explore the Celtic origins of the holiday and the traditions that shaped it. Participants will learn about the lunar-based Celtic Tree Astrology system and discover which “tree” aligns with their birth cycle. Rangers will also guide a hands-on tree identification activity using bark and leaf characteristics from common Staten Island species. Costumes encouraged.
events.venue: Martling Avenue and Brooks Pond Place (in Clove Lakes Park)

events.title: Fantasy Forest Immersive Hike: Alien Visitors
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers for an afternoon of local stories and memorable park legends, including the Staten Island Advance’s report of an unusual encounter in Blue Heron Park. Take part in an immersive group activity that retraces moments from the reported sighting and explores how these tales become part of community lore.
events.venue: Blue Heron Nature Center (in Blue Heron Park)

events.title: Birding: Fall Migration
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers on an exclusive tour of the closed Edgemere Landfill to bid farewell to birds migrating south for the winter and welcome our winter residents completing their journeys from the north, such as migratory waterfowl and songbirds.
events.venue: Beach 54th and Almeda Avenue (in Rockaway Community Park)

events.title: Open House New York: Fort Totten
events.description: Its Open House New York Weekend! This hidden gem was a military base for over 100 years. Explore the many historic structures of the peninsula and learn about the important role Fort Totten played in New York City’s defense history, from the Civil War to today. Visit OHNY to register.
events.venue: Fort Totten Front Gate (in Fort Totten Park)

events.title: Outdoor Skills: Orienteering and Navigation Skills
events.description: Do you have a bad sense of direction and want to get better? Do you always know your way on city streets but worry you’d get lost in the woods? Join the Urban Park Rangers to try your hand at Orienteering! Orienteering is an adventurous map sport in which a participant uses maps of a landscape to find a series of locations on a course, combining hiking and navigation skills.
events.venue: Alley Pond Adventure Course (in Alley Pond Park)

events.title: Open House New York: Fort Totten
events.description: Its Open House New York Weekend! This hidden gem was a military base for over 100 years. Explore the many historic structures of the peninsula and learn about the important role Fort Totten played in New York City’s defense history, from the Civil War to today. Visit OHNY to register.
events.venue: Fort Totten Front Gate (in Fort Totten Park)

events.title: Halloween: Wags to Witches
events.description: SAVE THE DATE!Get ready for creepy crafts, face painting, spine-chilling stories and more!Event will be held on the lawn of the Van Cortlandt House Museum.Join us at 3pm for our Third Annual Pup Parade & Canine Costume Contest.Register your pup day-of between 2pm and 2:45pm, or pre-register opening soon.Join the Urban Park Rangers for Nocturnal Creatures and Wildlife Hike leaving the Nature Center at 6pm and returning at 7:30pm.More details here.
events.venue: Van Cortlandt House Museum (in Van Cortlandt Park)

events.title: 2026 Spooky Snug Harbor Tour
events.description: Snug Harbor is one of Staten Island’s most beautiful historic destinations. And, if the legends are true, one of its most haunted… This fall, join us for “Spooky Snug Harbor,” a series of nighttime walking tours aimed at shedding light on Snug Harbor’s darkest history. Guided by local history enthusiast Michael Pelczar, founder of Spooky Staten Island, your tour group will hear never-before-published information. Visitors will also have the opportunity to use ghost-hunting equipment during each tour session. Can we make contact with the other side? On October 31st 9:00-10:30 Join our Halloween Special Spooky Snug Harbor tour, you'll journey back in time to learn about murder, mayhem, and hauntings at Snug. You will visit the final resting place of Captain Robert Randall, whose wealth willed Snug Harbor into existence. You'll ponder the mystery of Chaplain Quinn's murder, a crime that gripped the nation. You'll learn about the 19th century disaster that rattled the harbor's buildings... and the unlikely reason its sole survivor escaped. You'll discover a disappearance that sent the institution into a frenzy, and so much more... When: The event runs from 7:30 PM to 9:00 PM. events.title: New Dendrology at the Arsenal Gallery
events.description: New Dendrology is a group exhibition featuring eleven artists whose work contributes to the study of trees, offering new insight and connection between humans and their arboreal neighbors.From communing with streets trees through a reading with The New York City Street Tree Tarot deck by Matthew López-Jensen, to the commitment ceremonies officiated by Laura Nova, artworks featured in this exhibition invite you to engage in a new kind of relationship with trees. Featured Artist: Mariel Collard, Karin Giusti, Mark Heller, Anya Hoyer, Ekene Ijeoma, Gail Karlsson, sTo Len, Anthoula Lelekidis, Matthew López-Jensen, Amanda Lovelee, and Laura Nova. Image credit: The Bright Oak, 2019, Matthew López-Jensen

events.title: Pelham Bay Park by Bike Tour
events.description: Have you ever wanted to go on a long bike ride in the Bronx but were worried about sharing the road with cars? Fret not! Join the Urban Park Rangers on a 9-mile bike ride through Pelham Bay Park that is almost entirely on dedicated bike trails. Bring water and a snack!
events.venue: Pelham Bay Nature Center (in Pelham Bay Park)

events.title: Nocturnal Insects Hike
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers on an evening of nocturnal insect exploration and learn about the many different insect species that emerge as sun begins to set earlier!
events.venue: Van Cortlandt Nature Center (in Van Cortlandt Park)

events.title: Magnetic Archery and Foam Axe Throwing
events.description: Our free archery class is a bullseye! Learn the art of archery with free lessons taught by our expert Urban Park Rangers. This program uses safe equipment with magnetic arrows and targets. All equipment will be provided. Foam axe throwing will be available for ages 5 and over.

events.title: Historic New York: Orchard Beach
events.description: Discover NYC's storied past with our expert Urban Park Rangers as your guide to historical events, people, and communities that have shaped our city and Parks. Join the Urban Park Rangers on a journey through time and learn the history of Pelham Bay Park’s Orchard Beach!
events.venue: Section 2 Orchard Beach (in Pelham Bay Park)

events.title: Nocturnal Creatures and Wildlife Hike
events.description: Did you know New York state is home to flying squirrels and nine species of bats? Join the Urban Park Rangers on an evening hike through Van Cortlandt Park to learn all about our nocturnal neighbors and their roles in our ecosystem.
events.venue: Van Cortlandt Nature Center (in Van Cortlandt Park)

events.title: Beginner Fishing
events.description: Want to go fishing but don’t know how or where to start? Join our Urban Park Rangers for free lessons! Learn how to properly use a fishing rod or cast a net. Our experienced Rangers teach the ethics of fishing and the ecology of our waterways. All equipment will be provided. Recommended for ages 8 and older.

events.title: Nature Exploration and Restoration
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers to walk along the newly opened trails of Spuyten Duyvil Shorefront Park, recently restored by hundreds of volunteers and stewards. The 6.6 acre park features a trail that leads beneath the Henry Hudson Bridge to a native pond, a watering hole for local wildlife and birds, while another trail leads to sweeping views of the Palisades. Learn about this ongoing restoration process and enjoy fall foliage as well

events.title: Tai Chi with Pin Pin Su
events.description: Tai chi—the ultimate mind and body workout, often described as “meditation in motion”—involves slow, fluid, continuous movements through formalized postures of centuries-old Chinese Taoist martial arts.This event is free and open to the public. All levels are welcome. Please wear comfortable clothes and shoes to move around in.Advance registration is encouraged. Walk-ups are welcome. The event will be canceled if it rains. The decision will be made by 5pm the day before and registrants will receive an email if the event is canceled.
events.venue: Under the Standard (in The High Line)

events.title: Brazilian Movement with Maria Assis
events.description: Come join us to dance on the High Line! Brazilian movement is a unique and fun combination of Samba reggae from Bahia, Rio de Janeiro, and West African and Latino beats. All levels are welcome.This event is free and open to the public. All levels are welcome. Please wear comfortable clothes and shoes to move around in. Water will be provided.Advance registration is encouraged. Walk-ups are welcome. The event is rain or shine—the event space is fully covered. In the event of extreme weather, this program may be canceled for the health and safety of our visitors and staff. If a cancellation is necessary, Eventbrite registrants will be notified via email and we will post an update on our website.

events.title: Spotlight tour: Architecture & Design
events.description: Take a deep dive into design and architecture—both on and off the park—with a 90-minute specialized tour led by a High Line Docent, a knowledgeable volunteer guide. In it, you’ll hear about the architectural and technological feats of the once-active railway, the 720 wild ideas once proposed for the High Line’s transformation during the Ideas Competition, the tenets that guided the park’s architectural and landscape design, and so much more.Design & Architecture tours will be led by Irene Buchman and Frederica Sigel on September 17, and Bridget Gramling on October 22.

events.title: Great Trees of Tompkins Square Park
events.description: Trees have a special place in our environment. Join us for a hike of Tompkins Square Park in search of different species and learn some ways to identify these trees during the fall season.
events.venue: Avenue A and St. Marks Place (in Tompkins Square Park)

events.title: Birding: Fall Migration
events.description: Our Urban Park Rangers will guide you to the best viewing spots in New York City to see fall migratory birds. Birding programs are appropriate for all skill levels and beginners are welcome. Join the Urban Park Rangers on a birding adventure around Riverside Park to look for fall migrants that include warblers, raptors and more!
events.venue: West 116th Street and Riverside Drive (in Riverside Park)

events.title: Autumn Starfest
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers and the Amateur Astronomers Association (AAA) at the annual Autumn Starfest! See Jupiter, Saturn, the craters of our Moon through telescopes supplied by AAA members along with star clusters, double stars, and other objects in the night sky. Weather permitting.
events.venue: West 218th Street and Indian Road (in Inwood Hill Park)

events.title: Open House New York: Mount Morris Fire Watchtower
events.description: A prominent feature of Marcus Garvey Park and its neighborhood, the historic Mount Morris Fire Watchtower serves as an important landmark for the Harlem community. Urban Park Rangers discuss the significance and history of this recently restored structure. Open access from 1pm to 2:45pm.
events.venue: Mount Morris Fire Watchtower (in Marcus Garvey Park)

events.title: Geology: Central Park Rocks!
events.description: New York City is the site of ancient earth-shaking and earth-shaping events. The bedrock that anchors the city’s skyscrapers tells a story of a place going back more than a billion years. The island of Manhattan is built on three strata known as Manhattan Schist, Inwood Marble, and Fordham Gneiss.

events.title: Open House New York: The Highbridge Water Tower
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers on a tour inside the iconic Highbridge Water Tower to learn about the history of New York City's water supply and enjoy the panoramic views from the top of the 200-foot tower Arrive between 1:00 p.m. and 2:45 p.m, to gain admittance. Registration is not required.
events.venue: West 174 Street and Amsterdam Avenue (in Highbridge Park)

events.title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
events.description: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies. Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.
events.venue: Conference House Museum (in Conference House Park)

He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies. Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.
events.venue: Conference House Museum (in Conference House Park)

events.title: The Garden People: 45 Years in Bloom
events.description: Since 1981, The Garden People have lovingly cared for this special corner at 91st Street in the heart of Riverside Park. What began as a grassroots effort by neighbors has blossomed into an iconic New York City landmark and a beloved refuge for community members and visitors. Join us as we celebrate 45 years of growing together and say thank you to the neighbors, volunteers, friends, and supporters who have helped our garden thrive. Enjoy an afternoon of live music and community amid the beauty of the garden.All are welcome. Come celebrate!

events.title: Sachet making + Community Engagement Tea
events.description: Stop by the garden for a tea tasting opportunity and herbal sachet making.

events.title: Pumpkin Painting at Newport Garden
events.description: Newport Garden and GreenThumb welcomes all for an afternoon activity! We will have limited pumpkins available for participants to paint. Come learn more about the garden and meet community members!

events.title: Fall Children's Harvest Celebration
events.description: Please join us for our annual Fall Children's Harvest Festival as we close out the garden with fun (and spooky!) activities. We will have games, face painting, a costume contest, dancing, food, arts and crafts. Come dressed in costume!

events.title: Open House New York: Gravesend Cemetery
events.description: It's Open House New York Weekend! The Urban Park Rangers will guide you through this landmarked cemetery that was established by Lady Deborah Moody in 1643 and is home to graves of early settlers and founding families of Brooklyn. Register at Open House New York.

events.title: Birding with Ryan
events.description: Join local birdwatching author and garden member Ryan Goldberg for a fall birding event. We'll check the garden's trees for migrating birds and the skies for passing hawks, and we'll also talk about birding in the city and the wonders of migration. Bring binoculars if you have them.

events.title: Wild Oyster Survey
events.description: Wild oysters are a key indicator of ecosystem health in the New York Harbor. Randall’s Island Park Alliance is partnering with the Billion Oyster Project to conduct a wild oyster survey in the Little Hell Gate Salt Marsh.Volunteers will have the opportunity to identify oysters and take multiple parameters to determine the abundance, size, and health of the wild oyster population. Be sure to wear clothing and footwear you don’t mind getting muddy! Volunteers will meet at the entrance to the Little Hell Gate Salt Marsh near the Asphalt Pad. Registration is required here.Location: Little Hell Gate Salt MarshFor inquiries about accessibility, to request an accommodation or for event information, please email publicprograms@randallsisland.org.
events.venue: Little Hell Gate Salt Marsh (in Randall's Island Park)

events.title: Volunteer Workday: Wanaqua Garden
events.description: Join Wanaqua Garden and NYC Parks GreenThumb for a volunteer day helping repair garden beds and paint picnic benches! This community garden is cared for by volunteers who are excited to meet you and share their rich history of environmental stewardship, urban gardening, and hosting community events. This is a great opportunity for anyone looking to join a growing garden!No experience necessary - beginners are welcome! We'll provide all the tools, training, and guidance to ensure a productive and safe volunteer day! Please wear sturdy work shoes and weather-appropriate clothing and bring water and snacks. Note some tasks will involve lifting heavy materials and extended periods of bending, squatting, and moving.Register here!For information about group volunteering, please contact the GreenThumb Volunteer Program at gt.volunteer@parks.nyc.gov This event is co-hosted by NYC Parks GreenThumb. GreenThumb community gardens are organized, led, and cared for by dedicated volunteer gardeners who critically upkeep them as public green spaces. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

Discover native plant communities unique to New York City, and how to support these ecosystems in our urban landscape. Registration is required. Visit Open House New York to register

events.title: Open House New York: Prison Ship Martyrs' Monument
events.description: It's Open House New York Weekend! Discover the history of this Brooklyn landmark that pays tribute to the 11,000 men, women, and children who died on British Prison Ships during the Revolutionary War. Registration is required. Visit Open House New York to register

events.title: Open House New York: Grand Army Plaza
events.description: It's Open House New York Weekend! Join the Urban Park Rangers and the Prospect Park Alliance for a special access tour of Prospect Park's Grand Army Plaza, including going inside the Soldiers’ and Sailors’ Memorial Arch and climbing the spiral stairs to the top. events.title: Tiny Dwellings in the Heritage Garden
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers for a hands-on garden workshop. Using natural materials gathered from the landscape, participants will design and build their own miniature fairy houses while exploring the heritage garden’s unique plantings. Rangers will share tips on growing native plants in New York City and highlight the stories hidden within this historic green space. events.title: Fall Foliage Canoeing
events.description: Few experiences compare with being on the open water in New York City. The rhythm of the waves, the sun on your face, and the exhilaration of slicing through the water all add up to an experience you’ll never forget. events.description: Interested in being a garden volunteer? Fill out our Garden Interest Form!Join us every third Saturday from 11 AM-2 PM for our Membership Meeting and Volunteer Workdays! This is a great opportunity to learn about how we care for and manage George Washington Carver Community Garden. This Fall, we're making exciting progress to redesign the garden so that by spring, we're ready for the new growing season!We'll be dismantling old garden structures and moving organic material to prepare for our special Halloween Volunteer Event** where we welcome everyone to come in their best garden-themed costume & help us build our new beds!Fall Schedule (11 AM-2 PM):September 19thOctober 17thOctober 31st at 10:00 AM**November 21stFor questions, please e-mail us at gwashingtoncarvergarden@gmail.com. events.title: Community Banquet Planning Meeting
events.description: Help us plan and prepare for the 5th annual Community Banquet, a yearly grassroots tradition highlights the plants and people of the Bronx River. Each year this event invites partners and friends to share lessons learned from the past year, reconnecting people to the land through FREE wild food and drink tastings, herbalism, educational workshops, art, music and more! Join these meetings and help shape the event, scheduled for November 7th from 12-4pm.

events.title: Sharing and Gratitude
events.description: Amboy Street Garden will be holding a day of Sharing and Gratitude. In celebration of garden manager, Tammy Hall’s, thirty years as a professional storyteller, gardeners are invited come hear and share stories, bring toiletries and clothing for a barrel to be sent to Jamaica to support a community greatly affected by the recent hurricane, and enjoy refreshments, harvesting and fun!

events.description: Volunteer with the Stewardship Team to plant trees in the forest of Kissena Park! Trees provide so many benefits to New Yorkers such as improved air and water quality, reduced pollution, and lower energy costs. Volunteers will be trained in proper planting techniques. Come dressed in sturdy boots or shoes, long sleeves, long pants, and clothing that can get dirty. Face masks may be worn at your discretion. events.title: Old Stone House: Open Hours
events.description: Come visit the Old Stone House during our public Open Hours! Suggested donation for entry is $3, but no one is turned away for lack of funds. No reservation is necessary for entry.Please note that while our typical hours are Friday-Sunday, 12-4 PM, we host private or ticketed events that may limit public access to the exhibitions. The times listed here are the most accurate reflection of when the House is open to the public. Join us in the upstairs Great Room for new Contemporary Art Exhibits every season.Downstairs we host our permanent exhibit: The Old Stone House: Witness to War: An Exhibit Exploring Conflict from Kieft’s War through the Battle of Brooklyn and the Occupation, 1643-1783Old Stone House: Witness to War is a self-directed exhibit that takes visitors on a journey from the Lenape village of Marechkawick through Dutch colonization and the Revolutionary War era in Brooklyn. Ten themed areas allow visitors to explore this history and consider how war and displacement impacted the community, what choices people had to make at the time, battle strategies, and what makes these issues relevant in today’s world. ACCESSIBILITYThe contemporary art gallery is on display in our Great Room which is up 18 steps with a railing on one side.Witness to War is on the ground floor. The doorway has a 1.5 inch threshold.Public park bathrooms are on the South side of the building. They are on the ground floor but are not currently wheelchair accessible.You will find many oppurtunities to sit and rest throughout the House.The history and art on display should be considered "PG" for complex themes.The atmosphere is always family-friendly and visiting us is a great way for children to practice respectful museum behavior.Tours and walk throughs outside our usual open hours are available by appointment, we'd love to accomidate you! Please contact us with any questions.

events.title: The Perfume of Grief With Julianne Zaleta
events.description: Join perfumer and botanist Julianne Zaleta for this hands-on essential oils and perfume class surrounding the theme of grief.Significant loss demands real attention to your well being. Having a scent to support you won't cure grief, but the right composition will help you acknowledge and commemorate, perhaps even celebrate, disentangling loving memories from the pain of loss. It helps you honor and celebrate your memories, while easing the pain that comes with longing for a lost loved one. Plants can help so much in supporting and building the heart to be whole again, helping us find strength, courage and relief. Explore the oils associated with healing emotional pain and create your own perfume to take home.alchemologie.com

events.title: 2026 Ocean Breeze Fall Festival
events.description: Celebrate the Season at Ocean Breeze!Join us for one of Ocean Breeze’s favorite community traditions — the 2026 Ocean Breeze Fall Festival, a festive day bringing families, friends and neighbors together to celebrate everything we love about fall!Ocean Breeze will come alive with family-friendly activities, interactive games, music, entertainment, community organizations, seasonal attractions and plenty of fall fun for all ages. Explore the festival, connect with local organizations and community partners, enjoy the sights and sounds of the season, and make memories with family and friends.And, of course, no fall celebration is complete without a visit to the Ocean Breeze Pumpkin Patch! Pick out the perfect pumpkin to bring home and continue the fall festivities with your family.Pumpkins are available while supplies last
events.venue: Ocean Breeze Athletic Complex (in Ocean Breeze Park)

events.title: Autumn Pollinator Garden Exploration
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers for a fall exploration of the Blue Heron native pollinator garden as the last blooms of the season fade. Participants will observe late-season pollinators still visiting the garden and learn how native plants and insects prepare for the colder months ahead. It’s a gentle look at how the garden transitions during the autumn season.
events.venue: Blue Heron Nature Center (in Blue Heron Park)

events.title: REIMAGINING: Fall Get-Together
events.description: The event will begin with a moving live performance by musician Juan Usera and The Sambuco Tribe, setting the tone and making space for remembrance and renewal. Following the music, Bronx-based artist Tijay Mohammed will lead an interactive chalk art project aptly named “Message to my Ancestors,” transforming the pathway into a vibrant canvas that honors history and sparks imagination for the future.Local artists will work alongside Tijay Mohammed, including Adrian Bermeo, Adrienne George, Dario Mohr, Musah Swallah, Noel Hefele, and Yoshiko Mori.This unique gathering blends art, music, and community in a powerful act of reimagining, bringing people together in a shared experience of creativity and remembrance.Tijay Mohammed's "Message to my Ancestors" project is sponsored by Bronx Council on the Arts and AnkhLave Arts Alliance, Inc.The event is made possible by the New York State Council on the Arts with the support of the Office of the Governor and the New York State Legislature. This event is part of Van Cortlandt Park Alliance’s REIMAGINING initiative. VCPA invites the community to reimagine the park’s Enslaved African Burial Ground site as a memorial space that fosters long-term healing and restoration. Phase 1 of this project was supported by a generous grant from the Mellon Foundation. Juan Usera is a fourth-generation Bomba practitioner and culture-bearer from Santurce, Puerto Rico, a community educator, researcher, college professor, musician, and performer. He specializes in Puerto Rican and Caribbean music and culture and has over 20 years of experience developing highly engaging cultural activities and arts programs throughout the New York tri-state area. Juan is the founder and director of La Tribu del Juey Sambuco (La Tribu), an Afro-Caribbean music and dance ensemble and arts in education company. La Tribu has been featured at Lincoln Center and El Museo del Barrio among many others. He is the recipient of a NYSCA Folk and Traditional Arts Apprenticeship Grant, City Parks Foundation grant, and NYFA City Artists Corps grant among others.Ghanaian-born artist Tijay Mohammed currently resides in Bronx, NY. As an artist he has a strong passion for exploring issues that affect community and humanity at large. His work explores the concept of 'excess' in the production and consumption of products, and offers a solution through the integration of materials reuse and up-cycling. Tijay has spearheaded workshops and community-oriented projects for esteemed organizations, including the Studio Museum Harlem, Brooklyn Museum, Sugar Hill Children’s Museum of Art & Storytelling, Children’s Museum of Manhattan, Wallach Art Gallery, Lehman College, University of Ghana, and Pinto Community Centre in Trinidad and Tobago.
events.venue: Enslaved Burial Ground (in Van Cortlandt Park)

Feel free to bring your own work gloves and water bottle.Be sure to complete your 2026 season waiver before you arrive at the boathouse. Inwood Canoe Club en asociación con Friends of Inwood Hill Park están reclutando voluntarios para limpiar nuestra querida orilla del río Hudson. Recogeremos basura para limpiar nuestra comunidad litoral. Proporcionaremos bolsas de basura, guantes de trabajo, junto con algunos guantes de látex y agarradores. Puedes traer tus propios guantes de trabajo y una botella de agua.No olvides completar tu formulario Smart Waiver antes de venir a Inwood Canoe Club.

events.title: Air Pruned Raised Beds 102
events.description: Join Connor Youngerman of Cornell Small Farms and the Bronx River Foodway team for a deep dive into how to harvest from and winterize Air Pruned Raised Beds (APRBs). Following on the initial workshop this past April, this session will come full circle on how to implement APRBs as a propagation strategy. APRBs have been shown as an excellent method for growing a suite of urban tree species and hold great promise as a tool for forestry practitioners in NYC. Participants will have the opportunity to harvest and prepare saplings from the APRB, transplant them, and learn about overwintering the beds as a strategy.

events.title: Tour the Historic Lawrence Cemetery
events.description: The Bayside Historical Society is conducting a free guided tour of the historic Lawrence Cemetery, the burial ground of one of Bayside's founding families. The cemetery's first burial occurred in 1832, with the most recent in 1939. Notable individuals who are interred here include Cornelius Van Wyck Lawrence, New York City's first popularly elected mayor, and Colonel Frederick Newbold Lawrence, former president of the New York Stock Exchange. In 1967, the NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission designated the Lawrence Cemetery as a landmark. History will come alive on our tour as we recount the stories of different members of the Lawrence family.Outside Meetup Location: This tour will take place at the Lawrence Cemetery in Bayside, which is located at the corner of 216th Street and 42nd Avenue. Please note:The site will require walking on uneven groundLong pants are recommended to protect your legsNo restrooms are available on siteParking by the Lawrence Cemetery is limitedThe cost is free. Please RSVP on the BHS website: baysidehistorical.org/events-1/lawrence-cemetery-tour-3

events.title: OHNY: Conference House Park Historic Houses
events.description: Staten Island, New York City, and the nation’s history and architecture are alive and present within the built environment of Conference House Park. On OHNY Weekend, in addition to the park’s namesake, the circa-1680 Conference House (Christopher Billop House), two other historic house interiors will be open to visitors. This includes the NYC landmark-designated Henry Hogg-Biddle House (circa 1840) with its front and rear two-story portico and the William H. Rutan House (aka The Rutan-Becket House) with its intact 1950s era kitchen, not usually open to the public. The maritime past of Staten Island’s south shore is highlighted by these wonderful historic buildings.Access to the historic house interiors require stairs. Trails, pathways, and sidewalks connect houses and may be uneven.Conference House Park may be reached by the S78 bus to the corner of Hylan Boulevard and Craig Avenue, or the Tottenville SIR station. A parking lot and nearby street parking are available.Open House New York Weekend is an annual festival that unlocks hundreds of destinations across the five boroughs for behind-the-scenes tours and special activities.

events.title: OHNY: Brougham Cottage Grounds at Blue Heron Park
events.description: Join the Open House New York 2026 Festival and explore the grounds of the Historic Brougham Cottage in Blue Heron Park!Located at 4746 Amboy Road, Staten Island, NY, and located within a wooded backdrop, the circa 1726 Brougham Cottage is a surviving Dutch H-frame home.Brougham Cottage survives as a rare example of the small vernacular farm houses that were once common in the 18th and early 19th century rural landscape and have all but disappeared. It is a significant example of Dutch-American design and a rare reminder of Staten Island’s rural history and its vernacular architectural traditions.

events.description: Join us for a hands-on workshop on Air Pruned Raised Beds (APRBs). This workshop is a continuation from one offered in the fall but is open to anyone. APRBs as a propagation technique is scalable, modular, and can be done in urban and rural settings with modest start up and input costs. This session will cover seedling harvest and planting, winterizing air prune beds (with or without seeds and seedlings), seed collection and storage, and enterprise planning. Previous topics including APRB design, build, materials, growing media, and seed sourcing will be briefly reviewed.Register on Snug Harbor's website here

events.title: BHS Castle Tour
events.description: The Bayside Historical Society is excited to participate in this year's Open House New York Weekend, an event spanning all five boroughs that celebrates architecture and design.On Sunday, October 18th, from 12:00pm to 4:00pm, we will be participating with free guided tours of The Castle in Fort Totten Park, which has been the home of the Bayside Historical Society since 1984. Built in 1887, the building was originally used by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers as their Officers’ Mess Hall and Club. The Castle is one of the finest surviving examples in New York City of Gothic Revival castellated architecture, and is a NYC designated landmark that is also listed on the National Register of Historic Places.Our staff will be on hand to give tours and talk about our beautiful building and its history, along with the history of the land dating back to 1639. Guests can also explore the Bayside Historical Society's newest exhibition, "Home Front and Front Lines: 250 Years of American Service," which explores the stories of northeast Queens residents whose service, sacrifice, and civic engagement helped shape the American experience.Light refreshments will be provided. RSVP at www.baysidehistorical.org/events-1/open-house-new-york-2026.

events.title: Book Launch: Graveyard by Kyle Kouri with Adam Wilson and Molly McGhee
events.description:
Join us for the New York City launch of Graveyard by Kyle Kouri (author of The Problem Drinker) and a celebration of fail sons. 

Featuring Adam Wilson and Molly McGhee; moderated by Chris Molnar

About Graveyard:

"...it was moments like these that I felt bad for rich people. They owned everything and built monoliths, but would never know the romantic interludes that took place in them when they were gone."

So says Stud Calloway, guest services agent, in Kyle Kouri's gritty, literary fiction debut. Written by the best-selling author of The Problem Drinker, Graveyard is an LA novel about kids who hate their jobs, and make terrible decisions, but somehow are having more fun than anybody else.

About the participants:

Kyle Kouri (@kylekouri on Instagram) received his MFA in Fiction from Columbia University. He is the co-founder of Slashtag Cinema, a film production company, and has directed and acted in several films and plays. This includes directing and starring in the award-winning horror short film Keep Coming Back, and acting in Family Movie, which premiered at SXSW. The Problem Drinker, his first book, is an LA Times best-seller. His first novel, Graveyard, comes out October 30th.

Adam Wilson is the author of four books. A recipient of The Paris Review’s Terry Southern Prize for Humor, his work has appeared in Harper’s, The New Yorker, McSweeney’s, Tin House, Bookforum, VICE, The Paris Review, and The Best American Short Stories among many other publications. He teaches in the creative writing program at Columbia University, and lives in Brooklyn with his wife and their two sons.

Molly McGhee is a novelist from Nashville, Tennessee, living in Brooklyn, New York. She is the Undergraduate Creative Writing Advisor in Fiction at Columbia University. Her work has appeared in publications such as McSweeney’s Quarterly Concern, The Paris Review, and The Guardian, among others. Her novel, Jonathan Abernathy You Are Kind, was shortlisted for the VCU Cabell First Novel award and named a New York Times Book Review Editors’ Choice.

events.title: What do we need from our leaders?
events.description:
Once a month, we bring together a group for an accessible talk on philosophy and some well-structured conversation, with wine and bites in a cozy spot in Harlem.

Our goal is to recreate the best undergrad discussion course you ever attended and help you meet some people who want to have conversations about things that matter.

This October we're hosting Robert Gooding-Williams, the Brooks and Suzanne Ragen Professor of Philosophy at Yale and author of In the Shadow of Du Bois. We'll spend the evening discussing the questions: 

> what makes someone a progressive?
> do the most highly educated and well connected people have a duty to serve their communities?
> ultimately, what do we need for our leaders in order for our communities to prosper?

Here's how the night will go:

> [30 mins] Wine, apps, mingling
> [30 mins] talk from the professor
> [30 mins] breakout groups
> [30 mins] Q&A with the professor
> [as long as you want] continue your most interesting discussions

No pre-reading required, we’ll have a cheat sheet with the main ideas. Come alone or bring a friend, looking forward to seeing you there!

events.title: emdash poetry reading
events.description:
Our incredible readers:
Nicole Alexander
Sol Cabrini
Blush Bullseye 
January Santoso

What is EMDASH? EMdash is a bi-monthly calendar of NYC poetry events that has been publishing as emdashnyc on Substack and Instagram since July 2025. EMDASH is comprised of Ash, Subin, and Jacob, who really like poetry.

The EMDASH team wants to create a form of community-building and collaborative, decentralized reading that will occur between our featured readers. What this actually means is something we are calling “poetry two-stepping.” Here’s the premise: between readers, you have to get up, find someone in the room you have never met and read them some poetry. We will have three rounds. You read them one poem, they read you one poem. The poems can be your own poetry, a poem you like, or one of the many poems we will print out and provide at the front of the room.

We are making it sound more complicated than it actually is.. come !! Be earnest !! There will be lots of free wine and good company

SECRET HINT also. if you want you can dress up car themed. Think cars. CRASH (1996). you know.

events.title: Jazz With Joelle (Halloween Edition)
events.description:
Welcome to my monthly jazz residency at Old Flings! Our next event is OCTOBER 15th at 9:30pm. This event is FREE and there is no drink minimum! This is a special event of Halloween themed jazz - costumes encouraged but not required!

 How the event works:  My trio and I will open the set with a concert of standards and originals. Then we will invite other musicians to play. If you know the song, feel free to get up and jam! There is no drum kit at the venue (for now), but if drummers would like to bring some form of portable percussion (a cajon, for example), we encourage that!  

To keep things flowing smoothly, I will keep a list of vocalists that want to sing. Singers usually call the tune, and instrumentalists will follow. It is HIGHLY ENCOURAGED you know the key of your song! If this is your first time performing at a jam session, that's amazing! Knowing your key is an essential first step. The order of the jam will alternate between singers and instrumentalists.  This event is intended to be a traditional jazz jam session, meaning songs from The Great American Songbook/standard jazz repertoire. However, I don't mind making exceptions! This is meant to be a fun, non-judgmental setting. At the end of the day, music is about coming together and making something beautiful.  

Because this event is free, we do ask that people (if you are willing and able) contribute a tip to the band. We accept cash, Zelle, and Venmo. However, if you cannot tip the band, it is completely okay - please still come!  Finally, we ask that during performances, you keep talking to a minimum. There is limited space due to the size of the venue, so we would like to save seats for those who come with the intention to listen and/or play. There will be set breaks in between, so there's plenty of time to mingle!  The jam typically runs until about 12:30/1 AM. However the bar stays open afterwards, so feel free to hang out.  

We're so excited for another beautiful event! If you have any questions/want to ask me anything in advance about playing in the session, message me on either TikTok or Instagram (@joellebensaid).  P.S. - if you cannot make this one, there will be another one in November :) Poster by the amazing Dani Donatelle! Check out their work: @dddonatelle

events.title: Bad Movie Night Brooklyn: Ernest Scared Stupid
events.description:
Bad Movie Night Brooklyn is back at Freddy's bar for an underseen 80s kid Halloween classic! It's Ernest Scared Stupid! Joining in to introduce the film and flex his Ernhistorian knowledge will be Brooklyn own Martin Monster! A staple franchise lost to time, Ernest has done it all across 5 theatrical films and 4 home video releases in his 10 year movie empire. But among them, Ernest Scared Stupid was considered an oddity. Deviating from it's generally grounded roots, the movie featured a legitimately scary villain and crazy special effects courtesy of the Chiodo Brothers (the team behind Killer Klowns from Outer Space!). Past films saw Ernest go to Camp, break out of jail, and help Santa. But this time, lives are at stake. Because this time, Ernest has to slay a monster!

Plot:
Hundreds of years ago, in a small town in Missouri, children were being snatched from their homes by a vicious man-eating Troll. Eventually, the town rose up and captured the troll, burying it deep beneath the Earth. The children never returned .. but the Troll was never to be seen again... Until now. Ernest P. Worrel, a dimwitted but good-hearted garbage man and mechanic, has accidentally unearthed the monster on Halloween night, starting a new spree of kidnappings. And according to the prophecy, only he can defeat the Troll once and for all! With the help of a kooky old lady (Eartha Kitt), his trusty dog Rimshot, and a band of neighborhood kids, Ernest is going to once again save day, and banish evil once and for all!

events.title: BRIC Jazzfest
events.description:
In alignment with BRIC’s year-long curatorial vision of bringing Radical Joy to life, BRIC JazzFest 2026 expands the circle of what we consider jazz and welcomes those who have yet to find their home within its tent. The lineup presents jazz as a collective experience, as regions to move through and music to dance to.

Across two nights, Arturo O’Farrill & the Afro-Latin Jazz Orchestra,Bilal, Mohini Dey, Braxton Cook, Sparklmami, Marcus Gilmore, Melvis Santa presents Gata Jazz, Takuya Kuroda, Salin, Tyreek McDole, and Laura Anglade move jazz into conversation with soul, R&B, funk, hip-hop, electronic music, rock, house, Afro-Caribbean traditions, Indian rhythms, Indigenous Thai instrumentation, and American standards. Together, they demonstrate that jazz remains most alive when it returns to its roots in freedom and improvisation while opening itself to new voices, new bodies, and new possibilities.

events.title: Swap Salon
events.description:
Bring a garment that needs a new home. Leave with something new to you. Meet community, share stories and make friends.

Swap Salon is a small, curated exchange of distinctive clothing, shoes and accessories at CrossRoads Café. It’s a space to explore dress, extend the lives of things already in the world, and discover what a piece might become on another body.

Here, value includes the meaning a piece holds: where you found it, how you wore it, what you repaired, or why you kept it. Contributions don’t need to be expensive or designer.

WHAT TO BRING

Bring as many items as you like, thoughtfully selected, clean and intact. Clothing, shoes and accessories are welcome.

Fast-fashion pieces are welcome if acquired secondhand, purchased at least three years ago, or worn extensively. A secondhand Zara find belongs here; a clear-out of recent, barely worn fast-fashion purchases doesn’t fit the spirit of the exchange.

WHAT TO EXPECT

Browse, exchange, meet people and share stories of wear. You’re invited to tell us about something you’ve brought or your experiences of mending, sewing, buying and collecting. Sharing is optional, and no elaborate story is required.

Sewing supplies will be available onsite for simple alterations you’d like to try yourself.

YOUR $20 TICKET

Admission includes participation in the exchange, access to sewing supplies, and a take-home card of principles from the organizer's forthcoming book Wearing Otherwise: A Guide to Dress Practice.

Swap Salon is a participatory exchange. The ticket supports the gathering; individual items are not priced for sale. Come with curiosity and pieces you’re ready to pass on.

Hosted by EPB
Sunday, November 15, 2026 · 2 PM
CrossRoads Café · 119 Knickerbocker Avenue, Brooklyn
Limited space.

events.title: October Bookclub “Monstrilio”
events.description:
What better way to celebrate Latine Heritage Month and spooky season than with a Latin American author's take on grief and monsters?

Join us this month as we discuss Gerardo Sámano Córdova's debut "Monstrilio," a dual-perspective literary/creature horror novel exploring grief, queerness, and acceptance.

A grieving mother tries to preserve a piece of her son by cutting up a little bit of his lung and storing it in a jar. Inspired by folklore and fueled by unimaginable sadness, she feeds and nurtures the lung until it becomes a living creature.

This book club is free and open to anyone wanting to discuss stories of those who have been historically underrepresented in literature. Can't wait to come together in community soon!

Also, we're using this month as a book swap opportunity since last month’s was rained out. Have any books you want to pass along? Bring em and maybe you'll find something new to come home with <3

events.title: Crimson & Gold: A Fall Walk in Central Park
events.description:
On October 24, we’re taking an autumn walk through Central Park, exploring some of the park’s most beautiful fall spots, iconic bridges, scenic paths, and colorful foliage. Join us for a relaxed afternoon stroll through the park, with plenty of opportunities to enjoy the scenery, take photos, and finish together at the Conservatory Garden.

📍 Meetup: Columbus Circle / 59th Street Entrance at 2:00 PM, by the M5 Bus Stop. We’ll spend 30 minutes mingling before beginning the walk at 2:30 PM.

Along the way, we’ll visit some of Central Park’s most scenic spots:

• The Pond & Gapstow Bridge - an iconic Central Park view surrounded by fall foliage, with beautiful reflections and photo opportunities.

• The Mall & Literary Walk - a scenic promenade lined with towering elm trees and a beautiful autumn canopy.

• Bethesda Terrace & Fountain + Bow Bridge - one of the park’s most iconic areas, with stunning architecture, views, and fall scenery. We’ll pause here for about 10 minutes.

• Cedar Hill - a peaceful hill surrounded by colorful trees and a quieter stretch of the park.

• Turtle Pond - a scenic spot with views of the surrounding foliage and reflections on the water. We’ll pause here for about 5 minutes.

• Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis Reservoir - a scenic stretch with panoramic water views surrounded by autumn colors.

• North Meadow - an open area surrounded by trees, where we’ll stop for a group photo. We’ll pause here for about 5 minutes.

• Conservatory Garden - a beautiful six-acre formal garden in the northeast corner of the park and the final stop of our walk. Feel free to stay and enjoy the garden before heading home.

🚶 Walk: Approximately 2.5 miles at a relaxed pace (~2–2.5 hours)

🍂 Tips for Enjoying the Walk:
• Wear comfortable walking shoes
• Bring water

It’s free to join. Everyone 18+ is welcome 🎉

📸 Stay connected: Follow along on Instagram for future walks, food crawls, and event highlights:

https://www.instagram.com/nycfoodies.club

events.title: ‘Zero Sum’ - solo exhibition
events.description:
Pushup Gallery is pleased to announce “Zero Sum” a solo exhibition by Elizabeth Sundahl opening Saturday October 17th, 6-9 pm, 17-38 George Street Ridgewood NY.

Sundahl’s work recontextualizes familiar materials like paper mache, beeswax, colored pencil, and found objects into languishing, dream-like landscapes and interiors. Here, Sundahl examines the ways value is exchanged, consumed, obscured, and redistributed. This will be her first solo exhibition.

events.title: QUEER PANIC!
events.description:
QUEER PANIC: that feeling when you spot someone across the room and completely lose your nerve. this party exists to fix that.

(tldr: this is NOT a stoplight party). here's how it works - everyone gets a random colored wristband at the door. find someone else wearing the same wristband color, and that's who you say hi to! the color doesn't mean anything specific - it's assigned at random when you walk in. it's not "red for romantic" or "blue for platonic" or "yellow for creative" etc, there's no code to it, just whatever wristband you get at the door. could be a new friend, a great conversation for twenty minutes, someone you end up dancing with all night, or something else entirely. you don't know until you talk to them, and that's the point!

everyone in the room already knows the deal, so there's no wondering if it's welcome - it's a built-in reason to meet someone new in the community, no matter how big or small your circle already is! the only rules: low stakes, no expectations, and an open heart 💗

on the decks: 7-8 - empty visions 8-9 - DJ girlcrush 9-10 - HEYFAYBAE 10-11 - masha latte 11-12 - R-DNA

P.S. this is a real party first - DJs, dancing, a bar. the wristband is just there to make it easier to talk to someone new 😌

P.P.S. entry is $10, pay at the door! all the tix sales go directly to the artists ✨
